newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., may have to cover aquarium losses.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., may have to cover aquarium losses.

text.p: The Florida Aquarium is projected to lose $2 million in operating costs by October, which may have to be covered by the City of Tampa's general fund, the Tampa Tribune reported Wednesday.
The payment would be in addition to the $4.3 million in debt service the city must pay on the $104 million of revenue bonds it issued in October to refinance the aquarium's construction debt.
The struggling facility has cut expenses by $1.5 million through November, but that was not enough to offset operating losses due to lagging attendence, the newspaper said.

The aquarium is expected to lose $1.2 million on operations by March 30, the close of its fiscal year. The deficit could rise by an additional $800,000 by Sept. 30, when the facility will convert permanently to the city's fiscal year, the newspaper said.
City Council Chairman Ronnie Mason said that before the city agreed to buy the aquarium and refinance its debt, it was led to believe operating costs would be covered by admission fees.
The Arthur Anderson consulting firm is studying aquarium operations and is expected to make recommendations next month.
Mason said he is willing to wait for the consultant's recommendations but wants assurances that private donors are paying pledges they made to keep the aquarium running.
The aquarium is run by a nonprofit board. Mason said the city may have to select new management or take the extreme step of shutting down the aquarium.
"We can't expect taxpayers to keep bailing this thing out," Mason said.
